claim: The Hejaz Railway was ordered by Sultan Abdul Hamid II in March 1900; its gauge is 1,050 mm.
Water, fuel and labour were hard to find in the remote reaches of the Hejaz; camels carried water, food and materials to the builders in uninhabited areas.
The section of the line south of al-Ula was built and staffed only by Muslims.
note: Christian engineers were not permitted beyond al-Ula.

claim: The line reached Madinah on 1 September 1908, a date chosen as the anniversary of the Sultan's accession; to meet it, some track was laid on temporary embankments across wadis.
The Hejaz Railway Museum opened in the Madinah railway station in 2006; the old railway bridge over the 'Aqiq valley near Madinah was demolished in 2005 after rain damage.
